summary: Iteration 9 — Final Phase 1/1B Lock verification. All four NEW FIXES verified green via 15 new targeted tests in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9_final_lock.py plus full regression (157 passed, 3 legacy skips) across the entire /app/backend/tests/ suite. FIX 1 (Admin contact masking): GET /api/users?role=CLIENT as ADMIN returns emails masked as 'x***@domain' with contact_masked=true; phones masked as '07*** ***nnn'; SUPER_ADMIN receives identical rows fully unmasked; non-CLIENT rows (accountants) are NOT masked for either role; no password_hash, card, or stripe_payment_intent_id ever appears in any response. FIX 2 (Audited reveal): POST /api/clients/{id}/reveal-contact as SUPER_ADMIN with a reason returns full email/phone and persists an audit row (user, role, client, reason, timestamp) surfaced via GET /api/contact-access-log; blank/whitespace reason -> 400; ADMIN and ACCOUNTANT -> 403 on both endpoints. FIX 3 (Mandatory blocks submission ONLY): with an OPEN mandatory client task, POST /api/cases/{id}/record-submission returns 400 naming 'mandatory item(s) of tax information outstanding'; once the task is COMPLETED the same call returns 200 and the case transitions to SUBMITTED. Critically confirmed the client dashboard, /api/auth/me, /api/cases, /api/tasks, /api/documents, /api/messages, /api/notifications and /api/my-actions all stay accessible (no 403/blocking) for a client with an open mandatory task — visually reproduced on the client dashboard (screenshot 01_client_dashboard.jpg): the missing items surface as an 'Action Required' card, not a gate. FIX 4 (Stage guard): request-from-client on a case in READY_FOR_SUBMISSION returns 400 and creates ZERO orphan rows in tasks, document_requests, or messages (before/after counts identical); requests from ACCOUNTANT_REVIEW/IN_PREPARATION/AWAITING_CLIENT/CHANGES_REQUIRED still succeed. MULTI-ACCOUNTANT ISOLATION AT SCALE: created 9 fresh clients + cases (3 assigned to Accountant A, 3 to B, 3 to C), verified each accountant's /api/cases contains only their own case IDs, direct /api/cases/{id} probes across accountants return 403/404, admin /api/cases contains all 9. Accountant C was created via SUPER_ADMIN POST /api/users (idempotent — 200 or 400 accepted). REASSIGNMENT WITHOUT DATA LOSS: A -> B via /api/cases/{id}/assign transitions ownership; A loses read access (403/404), B gains 200; tasks created by A are still visible to B via /api/tasks?case_id=; /api/cases/{id}/activity retains full history; /api/cases/{id}/assignments returns >=2 entries including both accountant_ids. FRONTEND SMOKE: all 6 role journeys (Client, Accountant A/B/C, Admin, Super Admin) render correctly at their expected landing routes (/dashboard, /work, /admin, /admin), no console errors visible, screenshots saved. Accountant C's workload shows 9 own-cases only (proves case-based isolation visible in the UI). Client dashboard visibly shows the 'Action Required' pattern instead of a block. STOP-GAP FINDINGS: none. NO product code was changed during this iteration — only the new test file and the local test_credentials record were touched.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1196 lines — remains above the 700-line split threshold. Consider extracting the workflow/case-lifecycle endpoints (lines ~278-700) into a cases router and the user/audit endpoints (lines ~1003-1090) into an admin router. Not blocking for lock, but worth doing before adding the MTD quarterly workflow.
phase1b.py is 806 lines — same split guidance applies (recommendations, payments, offers likely fit as separate submodules).

assign_case (line 321) is used for both first assignment and reassignment. It writes to db.assignments AND transitions the case to ASSIGNED regardless of whether the previous status was ACCOUNTANT_REVIEW/IN_PREPARATION. This is functionally fine and preserves history, but ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS does not include IN_PREPARATION -> ASSIGNED — reassigning a case that's already in IN_PREPARATION would be rejected by the workflow guard. Confirmed via ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS map: IN_PREPARATION -> [AWAITING_CLIENT, IN_PREPARATION, READY_FOR_ADMIN_REVIEW, ASSIGNED] — actually ASSIGNED is in the allow list. All good.

record_submission (server.py:589) reads `mandatory: True` from tasks; existing task rows created BEFORE this feature landed default to False (no schema migration required). New rows always carry the field. Safe as-is.
reveal_contact (server.py:1015) trims-checks reason with a manual .strip() — good; consider a Pydantic validator on ReasonIn to also reject len < 5 in future if you want stricter audit quality.
No hard-coded lowercase pending/approved strings in the FIX 3 error message — good.
clean() strips password_hash defensively at the DB boundary — verified no endpoint returns it for any role.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All iteration 1-8 tests remain green under the fixed pytest.ini `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. New test file uses direct pymongo for a couple of state-planting operations (via os.environ MONGO_URL/DB_NAME) — dotenv is loaded at the top of the file so that works whether pytest is launched from /app/backend or /app. When adding future tests that need to reach RFS quickly, reuse the _drive_to_rfs helper — it uses the correct submit-for-admin-review checklist keys (client_information_reviewed / required_documents_reviewed / income_checked / allowable_expenses_checked / tax_calculation_checked / supporting_documents_attached / return_ready). Reassignment uses POST /api/cases/{id}/assign (not /reassign) — the server writes assignments history on every call so no separate endpoint is needed.
rca of the issue: No new defects found. The four fixes shipped in this round address exactly the reported requirements without side effects. The initial test failures I hit during test authoring were all in the test scaffolding itself (wrong client endpoints — /my-cases doesn't exist, must use /api/cases; wrong submit-for-admin-review payload — needs full checklist dict; wrong reassign endpoint — must use /api/cases/{id}/assign; pytest-xdist race on the module-scoped Accountant C fixture — solved by accepting 200 OR 400 as idempotent create). None of these indicated product defects.
